The one object named to the link is mingw-w64 gcc's build of `__attribute__((weak)) int dss_tentative = 5;`, a WEAK EXTERNAL over a body of its own (`.weak.dss_tentative.`), an OVERRIDABLE definition; the PE documents' `commonYieldsTo: nonOverridableDefinition` keeps the common over it, and the program reads 0, exit 37 -- the answer GNU ld gives mingw-w64 gcc's own common beside the same object (✔MEASURED 2026-10-08, both orders), on the same format where cl's select-any replaces DSS's common (`examples/c/dss_common_beside_a_selectany_definition_pe`). This example pins the RANK of a common DSS writes, not the form: a zero-filled strong definition (what the unit wrote before P69 fold 3b) also outranks a weak external and also reads 0. The `release` arm pins that optimizing the unit changes nothing about which of the two the program reads.
